readings.moment: The temple struck nine, when the husband had everyone show their watches at dinner.
When the temple struck nine at dinner, Félix's watch showed twenty minutes to nine.
The temple struck ten while she was in the salon.
When the temple struck ten, the salon clock showed five minutes to ten.
The doctor went out to fetch his cigars at twenty-eight minutes past ten by the salon clock.
A moment after the doctor came back, the hall clock struck eleven.

durations: Félix's father's silver watch had run badly for ten years.
Casimir and Madame Monnier have played piquet on Sunday evenings for thirty years.
The husband's repeater had taken four years of work.
Madame Monnier was married to Aurèle for thirty years.
A moment after the doctor came back, the hall clock struck eleven.
whereabouts: Madame Monnier dined with the others at the table on the evening in question.
The husband held out his hand at the table at nine o'clock and checked each diner's watch, with his napkin on his knee.
Félix was at dinner, where Aurèle scolded him in front of everyone.
Monsieur Girard and Aurèle quarrelled about the repeater at dinner.
Madame Monnier and Casimir played piquet in the salon without a break.
Madame Monnier looked at the salon clock in the salon when the temple struck ten.
The doctor left the room to fetch his cigars, which he had left in his coat.
The doctor went out at 10:28 by the salon clock.
Madame Monnier sat down at the piano at once when the doctor asked her to play, and played Chopin until he returned.
Madame Monnier stopped playing when the doctor came into the room.
The doctor came back to the room after going out for his cigars.
Madame Monnier says she should like to go up to her room (stated wish, not confirmed as done).
